messages.content: 創建一個藍色背景的正方形畫作，尺寸為16x16英吋，然後以70％的屏幕亮度顯示30秒。

function.name: painting_create
function.description: Creates a new painting with specified parameters Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

shape.description: Shape of the painting to be created.

dimensions.description: Dimensions of the painting in inches.

function.name: display_set_screen_brightness
function.description: Sets the screen brightness for viewing the painting Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

duration.description: Duration to maintain the brightness level in seconds.

function.name: painting_display
function.description: Displays a created painting for a specific amount of time Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to create a blue background square painting size 16x16 inches and then set screen brightness at 70% for duration? They want to show it for 30 seconds.

We have three functions:

1) painting_create(shape, background_color, dimensions)
2) display_set_screen_brightness(percentage,duration)
3) painting_display(time)

But we need to call them appropriately. The order likely: first paint creation, second set brightness, third display painting.

However, note that "display_set_screen_brightness" has parameter "duration". That might refer to how long to keep brightness; but they also ask to display painting for 30 sec. So maybe we should set brightness for 30 secs as well. But we can do separate calls: one sets brightness for some period (maybe indefinite or same). Then painting_display shows painting for 30s.

Thus steps:
Call painting_create shape="square", background_color="blue", dimensions=[16,16].
Then call display_set_screen_brightness percentage=70, duration=30.
Finally call painting_display time=30.

Let's produce JSON calls accordingly. Use tool invocation format. We'll output each call sequentially.
